unit.why: A memorate, passed on through a named chain of tellers at a siyum, depicting the Maggid of Kozienice's daily prayer and his own words about it.

stories.start_quote: עו״ש ממה שכ׳ הרה״ג אבד״ק סעראצק שי׳
stories.end_quote: ע״כ נותן לי זאת. ומי יודע העונש
stories.summary_en: At an 1860 Torah-scroll siyum in Charzel, tellers describe how the Maggid of Kozienice began prayer each morning in a faint voice out of awe, then cried out so loudly that he overwhelmed his listeners; the Maggid himself said that prayer was his only pleasure in this world.

quotes: בכל בוקר קודם התפלה אמר מי אנכי שאזכה
tags.why: The Maggid's manner of daily prayer is the subject.
The tale is explicitly about the Maggid's awe of God.
His prayer is described as cleaving to God.

quotes: עד שהוציא את השומעים מעשתנותם ולבם
tags.why: His prayer rises to a fervent, loud outcry.
He opens prayer by asking who he is to merit it.

quotes: הי' אתנו בחארזיל על סיום ס"ת
ואז סיפר לי הה״ג מו״ה דוד אבד״ק חארזיל
tags.why: The account is framed as told at a gathering, through a chain of tellers.
The point of the account is to illustrate the Maggid's awe and piety in prayer.

quotes: שאין לי שום הנאה מענייני הגשמיים
tags.why: He claims no pleasure from material things; this is borderline.
